_note: Illustrative VALID Round 2 case (input + hidden key bundled here for the fixture/test only). In real authoring, input and key live in SEPARATE files.

input.businessProblem: A specialty manufacturer's gross margin has compressed for four straight quarters while input costs climb; the owner wants to know the real driver before changing prices.

evidence.finding: Gross margin declined from 42% to 31% across four consecutive quarters
Per-unit COGS rose 18% year over year, concentrated in two raw materials
Throughput and scrap rates held steady this period; no capacity constraint observed
Competitor list prices roughly stable; no significant share shift reported in the segment

key.documented_root_cause: Input-cost inflation outpacing price adjustments; margin compression is cost-driven, not volume-driven.
key.expected_first_action: Decompose cost drivers and identify reversible margin-recovery levers before any price change
unsafe_first_actions: Blanket across-the-board price hike without elasticity data
